edgeSource.note: edges sorted by (source, target); directed, two-way streets appear in both directions

edgeLength.note: true length of the (simplified) edge in metres

edgeSpeed.note: OSM maxspeed where tagged (mph converted), else class default [88,64,48,48,40,40,32]

edgeTravelTime.note: length / speed, free-flow, no intersection delay

edgeOneway.note: 1 if the OSM way is one-way (no reverse edge), 0 for two-way streets

edgeReverse.note: index of the opposite-direction edge, 4294967295 if none (one-way)

nodeEdgeOffsets.note: CSR: out-edges of node i are edges nodeEdgeOffsets[i]..nodeEdgeOffsets[i+1]-1

edgeVertices.note: edge polyline lon/lat, oriented source -> target

properties.description: OpenStreetMap driveable street network clipped to the City of Chicago, simplified (degree-2 nodes merged), largest strongly connected component. Directed edges, CSR-sorted by source.
storyNotes: 29,557 intersections and 77,140 directed edges (27,799 two-way street pairs plus 21,542 one-way edges); 10,323 directed km of road in the largest strongly connected component.
Directed km by class: motorway 432, trunk 38, primary 230, secondary 1,686, tertiary 1,298, residential 6,478, service/other 161.
The Chicago grid shows: 4,541 four-way intersections (15% of nodes with 4 out-edges).
Expressways (I-90/94 Dan Ryan and Kennedy, I-55 Stevenson, I-290 Eisenhower) are modelled as motorway edges and are the fast corridors for isochrones.
Median edge length 102 m, longest 5,049 m.
